decisions.reason: As a newly launched drainage line with its own webpage, Product A reflects visible investment and a public commitment in a core technical area, so management is likely to persist.
Product B fits the firm's stated move toward floor-level, integrated bathroom drainage systems, so despite its recent launch management would strongly justify continuing it.
Because Product C supports the firm's design-conscious positioning and was important enough to receive its own page, management is likely to keep backing it after only one year.
Product D closely matches the firm's promise of installation ease and integrated solutions, making withdrawal unlikely while recent investments are still being defended.

Although slightly less central to the firm's forward-looking shower focus, Product E still sits within its drainage competence and has visible market presentation, so management would probably continue it.

Product F appears the most peripheral and less visibly promoted, but as a fresh launch in a technical product family management would still tend to attribute any weak traction to temporary causes and keep it for now.
